speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a chronic wound on your right lower leg; can you tell me how long it has been present and if there is any history of venous insufficiency or varicose veins? REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, ESR, CRP. REQUEST IMAGES: Right lower leg wound photograph.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count: WBC Within normal limits, Hemoglobin Within normal limits, Platelets Within normal limits; ESR: NORMAL READINGS; CRP: NORMAL READINGS.

speaker: Patient
text: 57-year-old male. The patient reports a large wound on his right lower leg that has been present for 6 months. He mentions that his legs have been chronically swollen for over 10 years and that his mother and brother had similar leg problems. He had a documented deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the affected leg 5 years ago but has no other significant past medical history.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Large wound on the right lower leg. I also have Chronic leg swelling, Family history of similar leg problems. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any discoloration, such as brownish staining, around the wound, and does the swelling typically improve overnight? REQUEST TEST: Venous Doppler Ultrasound. REQUEST IMAGES: Close-up of wound edges and surrounding skin pigmentation.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Venous Doppler Ultrasound: Evidence of venous reflux and obstruction in superficial and deep venous systems of the right leg; Skin examination: Discolored skin around the wound with evidence of chronic changes such as pigmentation.
